explanation: In modern C++, operator overloading allows defining custom behaviors for operators when applied to user-defined types or standard library containers. Specifically, comparison operators (==, !=, <, >, <=, >=) can be overloaded or utilized to compare containers for equality or ordering. These operators enable intuitive, readable code for container comparisons, provided the containers are of the same type and contain comparable elements. The standard library defines these operators for many containers, facilitating expressive and concise code that leverages C++'s strong type system and operator overloading capabilities.
